entries.proposition: The osmotic pumps contained vehicle, apocynin 150 micromolar, roscovitine 100 micromolar or Mdivi-1 50 micromolar.
entries.snippet: containing (1) vehicle, (2) apocynin (150 μM), (3) roscovitine (100 μM) or (4) Mdivi-1 (50 μM)

entries.proposition: The authors state, without data, that in a pilot and an earlier study these concentrations did not affect seizure latency or severity after pilocarpine.
entries.snippet: In a pilot study and our previous study (Hyun et al., 2017), the concentration of each compound could not affect the seizure latency and its severity in response to pilocarpine.

entries.proposition: Six hours after status epilepticus 81.7 percent of PV cells carried CDK5-Y15 phosphorylation against 19.6 percent in controls.
entries.snippet: 19.6% of PV cells contained CDK5-Y15 phosphorylation in control animals (Figures 4A,B). Six hour after SE, the phosphorylation of CDK5-tyrosine (Y) 15 site was significantly elevated only in PV cells. Thus, 81.7% of PV cells contained CDK5-Y15 phosphorylation
entries.anchor: Results / p47Phox-Mediated CDK5 Activation in PV Cell Following SE

entries.proposition: Roscovitine attenuated status-epilepticus-induced PV cell loss without altering p47Phox expression.
entries.snippet: roscovitine attenuated SE-induced PV cell loss without altered p47Phox expression in PV cells (p < 0.05 vs. vehicle, Figures 5A–D)
entries.anchor: Results / p47Phox-Mediated CDK5 Activation in PV Cell Following SE

entries.proposition: The roscovitine panel legend gives n = 7 per group.
The authors say that PV cell loss allows uncontrolled discharges and is a cause of epileptogenic processes, citing earlier work.
entries.snippet: Thus, the PV cell loss allows the development of uncontrolled discharges and one of important causes of epileptogenic processes (Sloviter, 1991; Sloviter et al., 2003).
